_note: SELFQ-RELEVANCE-1108 (owner 2026-11-08: typos such as 'vrea vrrea vra rvea vare' should trigger a clarification round). Before routing, help scoring or any search, the first question content word known to neither the stored-document vocabulary, the help vocabulary nor the A-P1 lay-term vocabulary gets up to max_suggestions nearest known words by Damerau-Levenshtein (optimal string alignment, transposition = 1). Never a silent correction. No suggestion within the bound = no pause. The vocabulary is derived from the corpora already loaded from the database and from the help data, never a word list. enabled=false: no pause ever.
_edit_bounds_calibration_note: PROVISIONAL (orchestrator 2026-11-08, from work/CALIB-ANALYZE-1108/report.md section 3, a simulation over the real vocabulary, not live traffic): words of 3 letters or fewer never pause (ties 82.5% at 3 letters; every 4-letter word has a neighbour within two edits, p90 156); 4-7 letters allow 1 edit; 8 or more allow 2 (79.5% of 8-letter words have a neighbour within two edits, p90 7). Simulated one-edit typos were 0% wrong at both bounds. Consequences: 'vra' (3 letters) and two-edit typos of 4-7-letter words ('rvea', 'vrrea') get no pause and are searched as typed. Calibration path: the request trace records counts only (clarify offered, suggestion count); review 2 weeks of live traces for pauses on correctly spelled words and missed typos, then tighten or widen per length.
_refresh_s_note: PROVISIONAL operating bound, not a decision threshold: the vocabulary is rebuilt in a background thread at most this often (and when a different corpus object is loaded). Chosen as 10x the acquired-corpus probe (serve.refresh_ttl_s 60) because building tokenizes every stored document. Change when build time is measured on the live corpus.
